content:
Over the past few months I followed a number of threads about slow docgen-action runs and caching problems: see docgen-action#3, docgen-action#28, docgen-action#33, #ecosystem infrastructure > huge increase in FLT doc-gen compile time, doc-gen4#389.

I did a sweep last week for some outstanding issues. Here are some problems and PRs to addressed them. In general they are about incrementality, either from local state or from the GH cache that the action reuses:

1) Locally, editing a docstring and rebuilding leaves the page unchanged (doc-gen4#389). The cause is in doc-gen4: the completion markers are empty files, so their Lake trace never changes, and the HTML step stays up to date even if the database changes. doc-gen4#418, ready for review, writes the hash of the dependency trace into each marker, so the HTML step reruns exactly when its inputs change. @David Thrane Christiansen I think you designed the marker thing, could you take a look? Also I think I need @Henrik Böving to approve workflow runs on my PRs.

2) Nothing removes the rows of a module that leaves the import closure (e.g. after a dependency renames it). fromDb builds its link index from everything in the database, so links can point at pages the build doesn't write. doc-gen4#416, also ready for review, restricts the index to the closure plus the pages already on disk.

3) On the docgen-action side:

  • the cache key is a hash of the manifest, so every Mathlib update is a full miss and a re-analysis of the whole closure (expensive with Mathlib)
  • the cache also stores dependency HTML, and a restored page of a module outside the current closure stays in the site and the navbar. The reasons to store the HTML in the cache are historical: i was the 'state worth keeping' before doc-gen4 moved the analysis into a database.
  • there is also a second cause of the 404s (a la docgen-action#33): the cache restores doc-data/, which has the HTML step's marker, but not the project's own HTML. So then when the marker is checked on a push that doesn't change any lean input the step is skipped (even with the doc-gen4#418 fix).

docgen-action#38 fixes this last thing by deleting the markers after a restore, so the HTML step runs on every build. It ports @David Renshaw's fix from his fork that some people have been using as a workaround.

docgen-action#40 improves the caching in general by storing only the analysis state: the database, the analysis markers and the bibliography data. The HTML is regenerated on every run (this is cheap enough). After a dependency bump, the action restores the newest entry of the same toolchain, so Lake re-analyzes only the modules that changed. It depends on doc-gen4#416 (to avoid stale antries), so it's still a draft...

4) Fast eviction is usally an issue: the docs cache entry is small (about 120 MB at mathlib scale). But lean-action saves the whole .lake on every push, and that includes the mathlib oleans it just downloaded, so each entry is several GB. A few pushes fill the 10 GB repo limit for caches and push the docs entry out, causing a full re-analysis in the docs step. People then interpret this as 'something wrong' with docgen (I saw this happen to multiple people already).

Setting use-github-cache: false on lean-action avoids it... maybe the docgen-action README should recommend it in its example workflow. Of course this means the project's own modules are rebuilt on every push (fine for a small project). There's lean-action#3 would make this better by excluding the Mathlib oleans from the cache snapshot.

Sorry for the slow turnaround on this one.

I took the liberty of adding a few tests and rephrasing a few docstrings on doc-gen4#418, and it's now merged. Thanks for this!

2) Nothing removes the rows of a module that leaves the import closure (e.g. after a dependency renames it). fromDb builds its link index from everything in the database, so links can point at pages the build doesn't write. doc-gen4#416, also ready for review, restricts the index to the closure plus the pages already on disk.

I also opened doc-gen4#421, which I think is a better approach to the problem solved by doc-gen4#416, and can also help out with the goals of your draft PR doc-gen4#419.

For a bit more info, doc-gen4#421 looks a lot like doc-gen4#419. The big difference is that it tracks files by package, rather than by library. I think this is less susceptible to corner cases related to orphaned modules being attributed to the wrong library.

Thanks a lot for handling these @David Thrane Christiansen. Of course I'll defer to your judgement on how to best implement these changes; my own judgement on the PRs was pretty much just about the tests making sense to me. On that same note, I opened a PR against your branch for doc-gen#421 with some tests that fail/panic in the current state (and their fixes for your consideration)
